''See also: [[Wei clan Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|The Wei clan is a prominent faction located in [[Sacred Valley]], characterized by its use of light and dream-based [[madra]] to deceive opponents. Founded upon the principle of serving honor through deception, the clan's identity is represented by a white fox symbol. Their territory features architecture in purple and white, inspired by the [[snowfox]] and [[orus trees]], including a massive white [[stone tower]] that serves as a major landmark. Historically, the clan was established by [[Elder Whisper]], who utilized the [[Path of the White Fox]] to assimilate smaller groups and dominate local [[Remnants]]. Clan life involves daily communal meditation and [[cycling]], which also serves as a forum for business and social competition. The Wei are known for their mastery of illusion and presentation, particularly during the [[Seven-Year Festival]] they host. Leadership has included Jai Patriarch{{!}}Patriarch [[Wei Jin Sairus]], a powerful figure who focused on his [[Path]] and often engaged in high-level combat or political threats. The clan's lineage includes notable members such as Kelsa{{!}}Wei Shi Kelsa, a strong [[Lowgold]] practitioner, and [[Wei Shi Jaran]]. While the clan has faced periods of [[destruction]] and relocation, it has also seen eras of significant expansion and influence, with some members rising to become Grand [[Elders]] or even Uncrowned{{!}}Uncrowned Kings.}}

== Unsouled ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-01-unsouled|Founded by [[Elder Whisper]] and the clan founders, the Wei clan is a massive group of over one hundred thousand people in [[Sacred Valley]] that operates under the motto 'Honor by any means.' Their culture is built upon the contradiction that deception can serve honor, a philosophy reflected in their use of light and [[dream madra]] to mislead enemies. The clan's aesthetic is defined by purple and white colors, inspired by the [[snowfox]] and the leaves of the [[orus tree]], with their banners featuring a five-tailed white fox. Led by [[Wei Jin Sairus]], the clan maintains an alliance with the Heaven’s Glory School{{!}}Heaven's Glory School and engages in trade negotiations with the [[Kazan]]. Members participate in daily morning meditation, celebrate milestones like [[Kelsa]]'s [[advancement]] to [[Iron]], and host large events such as the [[Seven-Year Festival]].}}

== Blackflame ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-03-blackflame|The Wei clan utilizes simple exercises to train their [[Unsouled]] members. Their spiritual practice follows a [[Path]] of [[dreams]] and light, overseen by a central Jai Patriarch{{!}}Patriarch. Educationally, all clan members are required to learn how to read before they begin studying their first [[Foundation technique]]. During various holidays and festivals, the clan celebrates by shining colored lights into the night sky.}}

== Bloodline ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-09-bloodline|Located northeast of the valley, the Wei clan is a group characterized by members who wear copper or Iron{{!}}iron badges and possess unique deep brown hair. The clan territory is protected by thirty-foot walls and gates featuring freshly carved doors from the recent [[Seven-Year Festival]], while a massive chain of scripted Goldsteel{{!}}goldsteel reinforces their boundary fields. Although the clan contains exiles and specialized members known as [[Irons]], they were recently forced into action by their elders when a [[Dreadgod]] waded into their lands. Following the devastation that left [[Lindon]] wondering if the clan had been crushed to rubble, he expressed a desire to return to them once he possessed great power.}}
